subject: Mathematics
prompt: Centre of a circle orthogonal to two given circles lies on their?
explain: Its power wrt both circles equals its own r², so the powers are equal and the centre lies on the radical axis.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Centre of the circle orthogonal to three given circles is their?
explain: Equal powers wrt all three circles puts the centre at the radical centre.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Circle centred at external point P is orthogonal to S=0. Its radius equals?
options: Distance from P to the polar of P
Distance from P to the centre of S
Length of tangent from P to S
explain: Orthogonality needs r² = power of P wrt S, which is the square of the tangent length from P.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Circle S₁ (radius r₁) is orthogonal to S₂. Power of centre of S₁ w.r.t. S₂ equals?
explain: Power = C₁C₂² − r₂² = r₁², since C₁C₂² = r₁² + r₂².

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Circle x²+y²=9 is orthogonal to a circle with centre (4, 3). Its radius is?
explain: d² = 25 = 9 + r², so r = 4.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: x²+y²+2λx+k=0 and x²+y²+2μy−k=0 are orthogonal for?
explain: 2g₁g₂ + 2f₁f₂ = 0 and c₁ + c₂ = k − k = 0, so the condition holds for every λ, μ.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Family of circles and radical axis
prompt: Family of circles through the intersection points of circles S₁=0 and S₂=0 is?
options: S₁ − λS₂ = 0, λ ≠ 1 only with λ>0
explain: λ = −1 gives the radical axis (a line), not a circle, so it is excluded.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Circle touching the x-axis at the origin has equation of the form?
explain: Centre lies on the y-axis (g=0) and the circle passes through the origin (c=0), so x²+y²+2fy=0.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Circle x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 touches both coordinate axes iff?
explain: Touching y-axis gives g²=c, touching x-axis gives f²=c, so g²=f²=c.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Line x/p + y/q = 1 touches x²+y²=a² iff?
explain: Distance from O to qx+py−pq=0 is pq/√(p²+q²) = a, giving 1/p²+1/q²=1/a².

subject: Mathematics
topic: Tangent and normal equations at a point
prompt: Circle x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 touches the y-axis iff?
explain: Distance of centre (−g,−f) from y-axis is |g|, so g² = g²+f²−c, giving f² = c.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Tangent and normal equations at a point
prompt: Tangents drawn at the two ends of a diameter of a circle are?
explain: Both tangents are perpendicular to the same diameter, so they are parallel.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Locus of midpoints of a family of parallel chords of a circle is:
options: a diameter perpendicular to the chords
a diameter parallel to the chords
a tangent parallel to the chords
explain: Each midpoint M has CM ⟂ chord, so all midpoints lie on one line through C perpendicular to the chords.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Circle S + λL = 0 has the common chord of S=0 and line L=0 as diameter. Then its centre lies on?
explain: The common chord lies along L and is a diameter, so the centre lies on L; this fixes λ.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Tangent length from origin to the circle on diameter ends (2,1),(4,1) is?
explain: S(0,0)=x₁x₂+y₁y₂=8+1=9, so the tangent length is √9=3.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: A circle is orthogonal to S₁=0 and S₂=0. It is also orthogonal to which circles?
options: Every circle of the coaxal family S₁+λS₂=0
Only circles through their common points
explain: The orthogonality condition is linear in (g, f, c), so it holds for every member of S₁+λS₂=0.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: A circle passes through two points that are inverse points w.r.t. circle S=0. It is ______ to S.
explain: Every circle through a pair of inverse points of S cuts S orthogonally.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Tangent and normal equations at a point
prompt: Number of tangents with a given slope m to a circle, and their relation?
explain: For a given slope there are two parallel tangents, at distance r on either side of the centre.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: For x²+y²=r², the chord with midpoint (x₁,y₁) has length 2√(r² − d²). Here d² equals:
explain: d is the distance from the centre to the midpoint, so d² = x₁²+y₁²; length = 2√(r²−d²) = 2√(−S₁).

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Limiting points of a coaxal system of circles are:
options: Point circles (zero radius) of the system
Feet of the radical axis on the circles
explain: Limiting points are the members of the coaxal family having radius zero.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Standard form of equation of circle
prompt: Circles concentric with x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 differ from it only in:
explain: Same centre (−g,−f) means the same g and f, so only c changes.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Standard form of equation of circle
prompt: Number of circles passing through three non-collinear points:
explain: Three non-collinear points fix g, f, c uniquely, giving a unique circle.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Standard form of equation of circle
prompt: Circle (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r² lies strictly inside the first quadrant iff:
explain: Distances h and k from the centre to the axes must both exceed r.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: For x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 (real circle) with c<0, the origin lies:
explain: S(0,0)=c<0 means the origin lies inside the circle.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Number of independent constants in x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 (so how many points fix a circle)?
explain: g, f, c are three constants, so three non-collinear points fix a unique circle.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Circles on AB and AC as diameters meet again at which point of triangle ABC?
options: Foot of perpendicular from A on BC
Foot of perpendicular from B on AC
explain: The foot D of the altitude from A makes ∠ADB = ∠ADC = 90°, so D lies on both circles.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Chord of x²+y²=r² joining θ₁, θ₂; α=(θ₁+θ₂)/2, β=(θ₁−θ₂)/2. Its equation is?
formula: x cosα + y sinα = r cosβ
options: x cosα + y sinα = r cosβ
x cosβ + y sinβ = r cosα
x cosα + y sinα = r sinβ
x sinα + y cosα = r sinβ
explain: The chord is perpendicular to the direction α, at distance r cosβ from the centre.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Position of a point w.r.t. circle
prompt: For circle S=0, points P and Q have S(P)·S(Q) < 0. Segment PQ meets the circle at how many points?
options: Exactly one only if PQ is a tangent
explain: One point is inside and the other outside, so the segment crosses the circle exactly once.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Position of a point w.r.t. circle
prompt: Locus of a point whose tangent length to circle S=0 is a constant k is?
options: A circle through the centre of S
A line parallel to a tangent
The radical axis of S and a point
explain: Tangent length² = S₁ = k² gives x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c−k²=0, which has the same centre as S.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Circles touching line L=0 at point P(x₁,y₁) on it form the family:
explain: Point circle at P plus λL; the radical axis L is the common tangent at P.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Locus of centres of circles touching a line L at a fixed point P on L is:
options: Line through P perpendicular to L
Line through P parallel to L
explain: Radius to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Chord of contact and pair of tangents
prompt: The chord of contact from external point P to a circle with centre O is ______ to OP.
explain: OP is the axis of symmetry of the tangent pair, so it is the perpendicular bisector of the chord of contact.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Chord of contact and pair of tangents
prompt: Distance of the chord of contact from the centre of x²+y²=r², for external P at distance d from the centre?
explain: Chord xx₁+yy₁=r² has distance r²/√(x₁²+y₁²) = r²/d from the origin.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Midpoints of chords of x²+y²=r² subtending 2α at the centre lie on:
explain: The midpoint is at distance r cos α from O, since the half-angle is α. For α=45° this gives r²/2.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Tangents at the ends of a chord of x²+y²=r² with midpoint M meet at P. Then OP·OM =
explain: The chord is the polar of P, and P lies on ray OM. In right triangle OAP, OA² = OM·OP, so OM·OP = r².

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Two chords of a circle bisect each other. Then both chords must be:
explain: A chord is bisected at a point other than the centre by only one chord; so the common midpoint is the centre.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Two circles of equal radius r, centres d apart, intersect. Length of common chord?
explain: Chord = 2√(r² − (d/2)²) = √(4r² − d²), since the radical axis bisects C₁C₂.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Family of circles and radical axis
prompt: A family of circles in which every pair has the same radical axis is called a…
explain: Circles sharing one common radical axis for every pair form a coaxal system.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Family of circles and radical axis
prompt: All circles x²+y²+2λx+c=0 (c fixed, λ varies) have common radical axis…
explain: Subtracting two members gives 2(λ₁−λ₂)x=0, so x=0, the y-axis.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Line lx+my+n=0 bisects the circumference of x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 iff?
explain: It must pass through the centre (−g,−f): −lg−mf+n=0, so lg+mf=n.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Circle has diameter AB. Power of any point P w.r.t. it equals?
explain: The expression is (P−A)·(P−B), and it equals S₁, the power of P.

subject: Mathematics
topic: Position of a point w.r.t. circle
prompt: Least distance of an external point P from a circle with centre C and radius r is?
explain: The nearest point lies on line CP, so the least distance is CP − r. √(CP² − r²) is the tangent length.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Tangents to (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r² parallel to the x-axis are:
explain: The horizontal tangents lie at distance r above and below the centre.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Locus of P from which tangents to x²+y²=a² are inclined at 60°:
explain: OP = a/sin30° = 2a, so P lies on x²+y² = 4a².

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Locus of centre of a circle of radius r touching the line ax+by+c=0:
options: One line parallel to it at distance r
Two lines parallel to it at distance r
explain: Centre is at distance r from the line, so it lies on either of two parallels at distance r.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Locus of centre of a circle touching two given intersecting lines is:
options: Circle through their point of intersection
Pair of angle bisectors of the lines
explain: Equal distances from both lines give both internal and external angle bisectors.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Number of circles touching all three sides (lines) of a triangle:
explain: One incircle and three excircles.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Two circles intersect at two points. Number of transverse (internal) common tangents?
explain: Only the 2 direct common tangents exist; transverse ones need d ≥ r₁+r₂.

subject: Mathematics
prompt: Circles x²+y²=1 and (x−1)²+(y−1)²=1 are in which position?
explain: d = √2, and |r₁−r₂| = 0 < √2 < 2 = r₁+r₂.
